skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Use the inference.sh belt CLI to search the web, extract page content, and ask direct research questions through Tavily and Exa.
skill.summary: Search the web and extract source content through Tavily and Exa using belt.
skill.author: qu-skills

security_audit.summary: The static external-command findings are Markdown inline code or fenced examples, not Ruby backtick execution in runnable skill code. The remaining real risks come from broad belt CLI permission and expected transfer of queries, URLs, and extracted content to third-party services.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the specific Tavily and Exa commands used by the skill, or require confirmation for other belt subcommands.
Add a clear privacy warning that queries, URLs, and extracted content may be sent to inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter.
Pin or verify the recommended CLI installation path, and explain that users should review the dependency before running npx commands.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The front matter permits Bash(belt *), which allows any belt subcommand instead of only the listed Tavily and Exa apps. This can run unrelated network-capable apps or account commands if prompt context is misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools line directly grants a wildcard belt command scope. The file later documents only a small subset of intended apps, so the permission is broader than needed.

semantic_findings.title: External Data Transfer by Design
semantic_findings.description: The examples send user queries, URLs, and extracted content to Tavily, Exa, OpenRouter, and inference.sh services. This is expected for the tool, but private data can leave the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented belt app runs include search queries, extraction URLs, and LLM prompts. These commands clearly use external services, though that is the intended capability.

content.value_statement: Research tasks need current sources and clean page text. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code requests through Tavily and Exa using the belt CLI.
actual_capabilities: Run Tavily search assistant queries through belt.
Extract readable content and image references from supplied URLs.
Run Exa search for relevant links and context.
Ask Exa Answer for direct factual responses.
Combine search or extraction results with LLM summarization workflows.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI to be installed and authenticated.
Sends queries, URLs, and content to external providers.
Does not verify every source unless the user asks for source review.
Quality depends on Tavily, Exa, and source availability.

use_cases.title: Prepare Current Briefings
use_cases.description: Gather current source links and summaries before writing a briefing or report.

use_cases.title: Collect RAG Inputs
use_cases.description: Extract clean web page text before adding material to a retrieval workflow.

use_cases.title: Check Published Claims
use_cases.description: Search independent sources and compare answers before relying on a public claim.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for [topic] and return the most useful sources with short notes.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Article Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract readable content from [URL] and summarize the main claims, evidence, and author context.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Tavily and Exa for [topic], compare source agreement, and flag outdated or weak evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a search on [topic], extract the top relevant pages, then prepare a sourced briefing with open questions.

output_examples.input: Search for recent research on battery recycling policy.
output_examples.output: A concise source list with current policy coverage, short notes, and recommended next searches.

output_examples.input: Extract this long article and summarize the key claims.
output_examples.output: Clean article text, a short claim summary, source details, and important caveats.

output_examples.input: Compare Tavily and Exa results for an emerging market.
output_examples.output: A ranked source comparison showing overlap, gaps, and sources worth reviewing first.

best_practices: Use focused queries with dates, named entities, and clear scope.
Review source URLs before relying on generated answers.
Keep private or regulated content out of search and extraction requests.
anti_patterns: Sending secrets, credentials, or confidential documents to external search tools.
Treating direct answers as final facts without checking sources.
Running broad belt commands that are unrelated to the listed search apps.

faq.question: Does this skill need an external account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the inference.sh belt CLI and any needed authentication for the connected apps.

faq.question: Which search providers does it use?
faq.answer: The documented examples use Tavily and Exa through the inference.sh belt CLI.

faq.question: Can it extract content from any URL?
faq.answer: It can request extraction, but access depends on the provider, page rules, and source availability.

faq.question: Is private content safe to send?
faq.answer: Do not send private, regulated, or secret content unless your policies allow those external services.

faq.question: Does it verify facts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It returns search and extraction results that should be checked against trusted sources.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
